newsitem.title: CHINA: China's major cities to ban leaded gasoline by 2000.
newsitem.headline: China's major cities to ban leaded gasoline by 2000.

text.p: China's major cities will introduce unleaded gasoline by the year 2000 to try to reduce air pollution caused by auto emissions, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.

The cities of Beijing, Shanghai, southern Guangzhou, central Wuhan and the boomtown of Shenzhen that neighbours Hong Kong will take the lead in fulfilling the goal of promoting unleaded gasoline in the next year, it said.
Beijing has already announced its plans to ban unleaded gasoline by the end of the century.

About 65 percent of the lead content in the air over Beijing is discharged by some 1.1 million autos in the city, it said. Beijing's Bureau of Environmental Protection has announced that about 300 petrol stations in Beijing's eight urban districts will be required to sell lead-free gasoline from July 1.
Unleaded gasoline will be used throughout the city by January 1, 1998, it said.
The southern boomtown of Guangzhou, capital of Guangdong province said its 900,000 motor vehicles used one million tonnes of leaded gasoline each year, it said.
The city's environmental protection authority had decided to introduce unleaded gasoline from October, it said.
